newsitem.title: UK: Exile group says Iraq prepared for U.S. attack.
newsitem.headline: Exile group says Iraq prepared for U.S. attack.

text.p: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein has ordered the dispersal of key personnel and evacuation of all major industrial facilities to reduce the impact of a possible U.S. air strike, an Iraqi opposition group said on Friday.

The Iraqi National Congress (INC) added that despite the dropping of an Iraqi threat to shoot at western planes patrolling its airspace, the Iraqi air force remained on full alert and Saddam was prepared to confront the United States.
The Iraqi Broadcasting Service, which is affiliated to the London-based INC, said in a statement: "Preparations for a U.S. air strike are taking place in Baghdad."
"Our correspondents report that all important command and control facilities for the army, Republican Guard, intelligence service and Presidential Palace have been dispersed," it added.
It said Saddam had ordered that no more than half the personnel of any military or security service headquarters should be in the same place.
All 70 operational combat aircraft of the air force were ready for action with another 30 being rushed into service, it said.
"Saddam Hussein has told Iraqi officials that he will continue the conflict with the United States," it added.
An INC spokesman said it stood by the statement despite Baghdad's withdrawal of its threat to western planes.

The official Iraqi News Agency said earlier in the day that Saddam's ruling Revolutionary Command Council "has decided today to suspend our military reaction (until further notice)...as of 2400 local time (2000 GMT)".
The United States has dispatched two aircraft carriers, plus Stealth aircraft and B-52 long-range bombers to confront Iraq, after it had fired missiles at U.S. air patrols.
